text: Jesus teaches that the Father knows what his children need before they ask. He sees what is done in secret in giving, prayer, and fasting, and rewards openly.
Jesus teaches that if evil men give good gifts to their children, how much more will the Father in heaven give to those who ask.
Jesus says not one sparrow falls to the ground without the Father, and the very hairs of his hearers' heads are all numbered. He tells them not to fear, for they are of more value than many sparrows.
Jesus charges his hearers to call no man their father upon the earth, for one is their Father, who is in heaven.
Jesus tells the Samaritan woman the hour comes when worship will not be at this mountain or Jerusalem, for salvation is of the Jews.
Jesus declares that true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for God is a Spirit and the Father seeks such.
Jesus thanks the Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that he has hidden these things from the wise and revealed them to babes.
Jesus says that with men it is impossible but with God all things are possible, and that as the Father raises the dead and gives life, so the Son gives life to whom he will.
Jesus declares that God so loved the world he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have everlasting life.
Jesus says all the Father gives him will come to him, and he will not cast out the one who comes. No one can come unless the Father draws him, and he will raise him up at the last day.
Jesus tells his disciples that the Father himself loves them because they have loved him and believed that he came out from God, and that the Father has committed all judgment to the Son.
As a boy in the temple, Jesus asks his parents why they sought him and did not know he must be about his Father's business.

Jesus declares that the Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand. All things are delivered to him, and no one knows the Son but the Father, nor the Father except the Son and those he reveals him to.
Jesus answers his accusers by declaring that his Father works until now, and he works.
Jesus teaches that the Son does nothing but what he sees the Father do, for the Father shows him all his works in love.

Jesus declares his judgment is just because he seeks not his own will but the Father's, and names as witnesses John the Baptist, the works the Father has given him to finish, and the Father himself who has borne witness of him.

Jesus declares his doctrine is not his own but his Father's who sent him, and anyone willing to do God's will can know whether the doctrine is from God or whether he speaks of himself, for he who speaks of himself seeks his own glory.
Jesus tells them they judge by the flesh while he judges none, yet his judgment is true, for the Father is with him.
Jesus tells his hearers they neither know him nor his Father, and that if they had known him they would have known his Father also.
Jesus declares his honor comes from the Father, whom they call God yet do not know, while he knows him and keeps his word.
Jesus declares that he and the Father are one, and bids his hearers, though they do not believe him, to believe the works that they may know the Father is in him and he in the Father.
Jesus asks for which of the many good works he has shown them from the Father they seek to stone him.

Jesus cites their law that says, you are gods, and asks why they call it blasphemy when he whom the Father has sanctified and sent into the world says he is the Son of God, since the scripture cannot be broken.

Jesus declares that whoever believes in him believes in him who sent him, and whoever sees him sees the one who sent him. He came as light into the world so that whoever believes will not abide in darkness, not to judge but to save.
Jesus declares he has not spoken of himself; the Father who sent him gave him commandment what to say, and his commandment is everlasting life.
Jesus tells the disciples that had they known him, they would have known his Father; from now on they know him and have seen him.
Jesus answers Philip, asking how he has been so long with them and yet not known him, and declares that whoever has seen him has seen the Father, so why does Philip ask, show us the Father.
Jesus tells his disciples he goes away and comes again; if they loved him they would rejoice he goes to the Father, greater than he.
Jesus declares he has not come to destroy the law or prophets but to fulfill them. He came to call sinners to repentance, seek the lost, and give his life a ransom for many.
Jesus declares the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins and tells the paralyzed man to rise and go home. He also names himself Lord of the Sabbath.

Jesus says every kingdom divided against itself cannot stand. He asks how Satan's kingdom can stand if Satan casts out Satan, declares that if he casts out devils by the Spirit of God the kingdom of God has come, and likens his work to binding the strong man before plundering his house. Whoever is not with him is against him.
Jesus answers the chief priests by saying he will tell them his authority if they first say whether John's baptism was from heaven or men.
Jesus tells the chief priests that neither will he tell them by what authority he does these things.
Jesus declares that all power is given to him in heaven and on earth.
Jesus asks the Pharisees if they never read how hungry David entered the house of God and ate the showbread lawful only for priests.
Jesus calls the man with the withered hand forward and asks whether it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath or evil, to save life or to kill. Then he commands the man to stretch out his hand.
Jesus says he has come to send fire on the earth and asks what he wills if it is already kindled.
Jesus says to his mother at Cana, Woman, what have I to do with you, and tells her his hour has not yet come.
Jesus tells the disciples he has food to eat that they know nothing of.
Jesus tells the disciples this man's blindness is not from sin but so the works of God can be displayed in him.
Jesus says this sickness is not unto death but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified by it.

Jesus asks whether there are not twelve hours in the day, saying one who walks by day does not stumble while one who walks by night stumbles. Then he tells the disciples their friend Lazarus sleeps and he goes to wake him.
Jesus assures Martha that her brother will rise again.
Jesus declares that no one has ascended to heaven but he who came down from heaven, the Son of Man who is in heaven.
Jesus says he came from heaven to do the Father's will — to lose none given him but raise them up at the last day.
Jesus tells the crowd not to grumble among themselves.
Jesus asks the murmuring disciples whether his saying offends them, and what if they see the Son of Man ascend where he was before.

Jesus tells his brothers his time has not yet come while theirs is always ready. The world cannot hate them but hates him because he testifies its works are evil. He bids them go up to the feast though he does not yet go.
Jesus cries in the temple that he did not come of himself but is sent by one who is true, whom they do not know.
Jesus says he is with them a little while longer, then goes to him who sent him. They will seek but not find him.
Jesus says he came from the Father into the world, and now leaves the world to go to the Father.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus declares that as Jonah was three days in the whale’s belly, so will the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus foretells that the Son of Man must go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, be killed, and be raised the third day.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus rebukes Peter, saying get behind me Satan, for he is an offense and minds the things of men, not of God.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus charges Peter, James, and John to tell the vision to no one until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus affirms that Elijah does come first and restores all things, but says Elijah has already come and they did not know him and did to him whatever they wished, and likewise the Son of Man will suffer.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus rebukes Peter, saying get behind me Satan, for he minds the things of men, not of God.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus says he has a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed he is until it is accomplished.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus tells the twelve they go up to Jerusalem where all things written by the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be accomplished — he will be delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, scourged, and killed, and the third day rise again.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus foretells he will be delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, spat upon, scourged, and put to death, and the third day rise again.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus drives out the dove sellers, charging them to take these things away and not make his Father’s house a house of merchandise.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus declares that as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus declares that the Father loves him because he lays down his life to take it again. No one takes it from him; he lays it down of himself, with power to lay it down and to take it again, as commanded by the Father.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus defends Mary — let her alone, she has kept this for his burial; the poor are always with them, but he will not be.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus announces that the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.

subcat: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection
text: Jesus tells the disciples beforehand so that when it comes to pass they may believe. The prince of this world is coming and has nothing in him, but so the world may know he loves the Father, he does as the Father commanded.
Jesus tells John to permit it for now, for so it is fitting for them to fulfill all righteousness.

Jesus tells John’s disciples to report what they hear and see: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor receive the gospel; blessed is whoever is not offended in him.
Jesus says that if his hearers will receive it, John is the Elijah who was to come.

Jesus defends his disciples by recalling how David and his men ate the showbread that was not lawful, and how the priests profane the Sabbath in the temple and are blameless, declaring that one greater than the temple is here.
Jesus declares that he is sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
Jesus asks his disciples at Caesarea Philippi who men say that he, the Son of Man, is.
Jesus presses the disciples, asking who they themselves say that he is.
Jesus blesses Simon Bar-Jonah, declaring that flesh and blood has not revealed it to him, but the Father in heaven.
Jesus reassures the disciples after the Transfiguration, telling them to arise and not be afraid.

Jesus teaches Peter that kings take tribute from strangers, not their own children, so the children are free; but lest they offend, he sends Peter to cast a hook and find a coin in the first fish’s mouth for the two of them.
Jesus declares that the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost.
Jesus sends two disciples into the village to find a donkey tied with a colt, loose them and bring them, and if anyone questions them, to say the Lord has need of them and he will send them at once.

Jesus asks the Pharisees what they think of the Christ and whose son he is, then citing David who in the Spirit calls him Lord — saying the LORD said to my Lord, sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool — he asks how, if David then calls him Lord, he is his son.

Jesus affirms that Elijah comes first and restores all things, and as written, the Son of Man must suffer and be despised; but Elijah has already come and they did to him whatever they wished, as it is written of him.
Jesus reads from Isaiah in the Nazareth synagogue and declares to the hearers that today this scripture is fulfilled in their ears.
Jesus tells the Pharisees that if his disciples were silent, the stones would immediately cry out.
Jesus greets Nathanael as an Israelite in whom is no deceit, and tells him he saw him under the fig tree before Philip called.
Jesus promises Nathanael he will see greater things — heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.
Jesus asks the Samaritan woman at the well to give him a drink.
Jesus tells the Samaritan woman to call her husband, then says she has spoken well in saying she has none, for she has had five husbands and the man she now has is not her husband.
Jesus declares to the Samaritan woman that he who speaks to her is the Messiah.
Jesus reveals himself to the healed man, telling him that he has seen him and that the one who speaks with him is he.

Jesus says the works he does in his Father’s name bear witness of him; if he does not the Father’s works, do not believe, but if he does, believe the works, that they may know the Father is in him and he in the Father.
Jesus announces that now the Son of Man is glorified and God is glorified in him, and warns his little children that he is with them only a little while longer; where he goes they cannot come.

Jesus tells the kneeling leper that he is willing and commands him to be clean, then charges him to tell no one but to show himself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded as a testimony to them.
Jesus answers the centurion's plea for his stricken servant by declaring that he will come and heal him.
Jesus answers the legion of demons begging to enter the swine with a single word, and bids them go.
Jesus, having opened the eyes of the two blind men, sternly charges them to see that no one knows of it.
Jesus calls the man with the withered hand to stretch it out, and it is restored whole as the other on the Sabbath.
Jesus calls for the five loaves and two fish to be brought to him before he feeds the five thousand.
Jesus asks the disciples how many loaves they have before he feeds the four thousand.
Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit in the Capernaum synagogue, charging it to be silent and come out of the man.
Jesus rebukes the wind and commands the raging sea to be at peace and be still, and there is a great calm.
Jesus charges the unclean spirit to come out of the Gerasene man and demands its name, which answers Legion, for they are many.
Jesus, perceiving that power has gone out of him, turns in the press of the crowd and asks who touched his clothes.
Jesus silences the weeping mourners at Jairus's house, declaring that the girl is not dead but sleeping, then takes her by the hand and raises her with the words Talitha cumi.
Jesus charges the disciples to give the crowd something to eat themselves and bids them go and see how many loaves they have, before the feeding of the five thousand.
Jesus looks up to heaven, sighs, and says Ephphatha, that is, Be opened, and the deaf man's ears and tongue are loosed.
Jesus declares his compassion on the crowd that has been with him three days with nothing to eat, and will not send them away hungry lest they faint on the way, for some have come from far.
Jesus charges the mute and deaf spirit to come out of the boy and to enter him no more.
Jesus asks blind Bartimaeus what he wants done for him, and at his plea to receive his sight bids him go his way, declaring that his faith has made him whole.
Jesus tells the weeping widow of Nain not to weep, then touches the bier and calls her dead son to arise.
Jesus tells the servants at Cana to fill the jars with water and bear it to the master of the feast, turning water into wine.
Jesus sends the nobleman on his way with the word that his son lives, healing the boy at a distance.
Jesus asks the man sick thirty-eight years at Bethesda whether he wants to be made well, then commands him to rise, take up his bed, and walk.
Jesus asks Philip where they will buy bread so that the great crowd coming to him may eat.
Jesus instructs the disciples to make the men sit down before the feeding of the five thousand.
Jesus tells the disciples to gather up the fragments that remain so that nothing is lost.
Jesus sends the man born blind to go and wash in the pool of Siloam, and the man returns seeing.

At Lazarus's tomb Jesus commands the stone be taken away, reminds Martha that if she would believe she should see the glory of God, lifts his eyes to thank the Father for hearing him so that the people standing by may believe the Father has sent him, then cries with a loud voice for Lazarus to come out and bids them loose him and let him go.

subcat: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
text: Jesus cries out on the last great day of the feast that if anyone thirsts, let him come to him and drink.

subcat: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
text: Jesus says he will pray the Father to give another Helper, the Spirit of truth, who dwells with them and will be in them forever.

subcat: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
text: Jesus tells his disciples he will not leave them comfortless but will come to them. Because he lives, they will live also; whoever has his commandments and keeps them loves him and will be loved by his Father, to whom he will show himself.

subcat: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
text: Jesus says the Holy Spirit whom the Father sends in his name will teach them all things and bring to remembrance all he has said.

subcat: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
text: Jesus tells his disciples it is to their advantage that he go away, for if he does not depart the Helper will not come, but when the Spirit of truth comes he will guide them into all truth and glorify Jesus.

subcat: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
text: Jesus charges his disciples to wait for the promise of the Father, declaring that John baptized with water but they will be baptized with the Holy Spirit, and that they will receive power and be his witnesses to the ends of the earth.

subcat: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit
text: Jesus says that John indeed baptized with water but they will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.

subcat: The Spirit's Work in the World
text: Jesus says if evil men give good gifts to their children, the Father will much more give the Holy Spirit to those who ask.

subcat: The Spirit's Work in the World
text: Jesus declares that it is the Spirit that gives life and the flesh profits nothing, and that the words he speaks are spirit and are life.

subcat: The Spirit's Work in the World
text: Jesus says that when the Helper comes he will convict the world of sin because they do not believe in him, of righteousness because he goes to the Father, and of judgment because the ruler of this world is judged.

subcat: The Spirit's Work in the World
text: Jesus tells his disciples he has yet many things to say to them, but they cannot bear them now.

subcat: The Spirit's Work in the World
text: Jesus says all the Father has is his, so the Spirit will reveal it; soon they will not see him, then will see him again.
Jesus says all manner of sin and blasphemy will be forgiven, but blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, neither in this world nor the world to come.

subcat: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
text: Jesus declares that many will come from east and west to sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, while the children of the kingdom will be cast into outer darkness.

subcat: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
text: Jesus says that since the days of John the Baptist the kingdom of heaven suffers violence and the violent take it by force. He warns it will be taken from those who do not bear its fruit and given to a nation that will.

subcat: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
text: Jesus proclaims that the time is fulfilled and the kingdom of God is at hand, and calls his hearers to repent and believe the gospel.

subcat: Nature and Character of the Kingdom
text: Jesus says the kingdom of God does not come with observation, nor will they say, Look here or there, for it is within you.

subcat: Growth and Presence of the Kingdom
text: Jesus tells his disciples it is given to them to know the mysteries of the kingdom, but not to others, and that he speaks to the multitude in parables because seeing they do not see and hearing they do not understand.
Jesus says that unless his hearers' righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, they will by no means enter the kingdom of heaven.
Jesus charges his hearers to seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, with the promise that all these things will be added to them.

Jesus charges his hearers to enter by the narrow gate, for wide is the gate and broad the way leading to destruction and many go in there, but narrow is the gate and the way that leads to life, and few find it.

Jesus declares that not everyone who says, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of his Father, and to many who plead their works in his name he will say, I never knew you.
Jesus says Isaiah's prophecy is fulfilled in them: hearing they understand not and seeing they perceive not, for their heart has grown dull.
Jesus declares that unless his hearers are converted and become as little children, they will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
Jesus says a rich man will hardly enter the kingdom of heaven, and that it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
Jesus declares to the chief priests that tax collectors and harlots enter the kingdom of God before them, for they did not believe John.
Jesus tells Nicodemus that unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God, and unless born of water and Spirit he cannot enter it. The Spirit is like the wind, blowing where it wishes.

subcat: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
text: Jesus blesses the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

subcat: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
text: Jesus blesses those who mourn, for they will be comforted.

subcat: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
text: Jesus blesses the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

subcat: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
text: Jesus blesses those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they will be filled.

subcat: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
text: Jesus blesses the merciful, for they will obtain mercy.

subcat: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
text: Jesus blesses the pure in heart, for they will see God.

subcat: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
text: Jesus blesses the peacemakers, for they will be called the children of God.

subcat: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes
text: Jesus blesses those persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven, and tells his hearers to rejoice and be exceedingly glad when they are reviled and falsely accused for his sake, for great is their reward in heaven.
Jesus proclaims that the time is fulfilled and the kingdom of heaven is at hand, calling his hearers to repent and believe the gospel.
Jesus says the healthy need no physician but the sick, and he has come to call sinners to repentance, not the righteous.
Jesus pronounces woe on Chorazin and Bethsaida, saying Tyre and Sidon would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
Jesus warns that an unclean spirit returns with seven worse spirits to the swept and empty house, so the last state of that person is worse than the first.
Jesus asks whether the Galileans whose blood Pilate mingled with their sacrifices were greater sinners than other Galileans.
Jesus asks whether the eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell were greater sinners than all who lived in Jerusalem.
Jesus says there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine just persons who need no repentance.
Jesus calls Zacchaeus to hurry and come down from the sycamore tree, for he must stay at his house today.
Jesus declares that salvation has come this day to the house of Zacchaeus, since he too is a son of Abraham.
Jesus finds the healed man in the temple and tells him, you are made well; sin no more, lest a worse thing come upon you.
Jesus asks the woman where her accusers are, then tells her neither does he condemn her; go and sin no more.
Jesus calls all who labor and are heavy laden to come to him for rest, bidding them take his yoke and learn from him, for he is gentle and lowly, and his yoke is easy and his burden light.
Jesus promises that all the Father gives him will come to him, and the one who comes to him he will never cast out.

Jesus tells Nicodemus that unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God, and unless he is born of water and the Spirit he cannot enter it, for flesh births flesh and Spirit births spirit.
Jesus tells Nicodemus not to marvel that he must be born again, for the wind blows where it wills—so is everyone born of the Spirit.
Jesus rebukes Nicodemus as a teacher of Israel who does not know these things, and asks how they will believe heavenly things if they do not believe the earthly things he tells them.
Jesus says some among his hearers do not believe, and that no one can come to him unless it is given by the Father.

subcat: Faith as the Condition of Salvation
text: Jesus declares that God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whoever believes in him will not perish but have everlasting life, and that whoever does not believe is condemned already.

subcat: Faith as the Condition of Salvation
text: Jesus tells Martha he is the resurrection and the life: whoever believes in him will live though he die, and whoever believes will never die.

subcat: Faith as the Condition of Salvation
text: Jesus urges his hearers to walk while they have the light and to believe in it, that they may become children of light.

subcat: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
text: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman that whoever drinks the water he gives will never thirst—it becomes a well springing up to everlasting life.

subcat: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
text: Jesus rebukes the crowd for seeking him over the loaves, charging them to labor not for perishable food but for food enduring to everlasting life.

subcat: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
text: Jesus says it is written that they will all be taught of God, that everyone who hears and learns from the Father comes to him, and that whoever believes has everlasting life.

subcat: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
text: Jesus declares that whoever commits sin is a servant of sin; the servant does not abide in the house forever, but the Son abides forever.

subcat: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
text: Jesus says he has no devil but honors his Father while they dishonor him, that he does not seek his own glory but One does, and that whoever keeps his word will never see death.

subcat: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
text: Jesus says the thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy, but he came that they may have life and have it abundantly.

subcat: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
text: Jesus declares that his sheep hear his voice and follow him; he gives them eternal life, and none can pluck them from his hand.

subcat: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance
text: Jesus tells his disciples that in his Father's house are many mansions, and he goes to prepare a place and will return for them.
Jesus charges his hearers to enter through the narrow gate, for wide is the gate and broad the way to destruction, but narrow is the gate and the way that leads to life, and few find it.

Jesus declares that not everyone who says Lord, Lord will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the Father's will. Many will claim mighty works in his name, and he will profess: I never knew you, depart from me.

Jesus warns that once the master shuts the door, those who knock saying Lord, Lord will hear him answer that he does not know them; though they protest they ate with him and he taught in their streets, he will tell them to depart.

Jesus calls Herod that fox and says he will continue his work until perfected on the third day. He laments over Jerusalem that kills its prophets, saying how often he longed to gather her children as a hen gathers her brood, but they refused.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus marvels at the Roman centurion, saying he has not found so great a faith, not even in Israel.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus tells the centurion to go his way, and as he has believed, so be it done to him.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus asks the two blind men whether they believe he is able to do this.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus declares that according to their faith it will be done, telling the bleeding woman and others their faith has made them whole and to go in peace.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus calls Peter out of the boat onto the water with a single word: come.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus says to the Canaanite woman that it is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to dogs.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus praises the Canaanite woman, declaring great is her faith and that it will be done for her as she wishes.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus tells his disciples that with faith like a mustard seed they will move mountains and nothing will be impossible to them, and whatever they ask in prayer believing they will receive.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus tells the Syrophoenician woman that for her saying she may go her way, for the demon has gone out of her daughter.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus laments a faithless generation and asks how long he will bear with them, calls the boy to him, and declares that all things are possible to one who believes.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus marvels at the centurion and declares he has not found so great a faith, not even in Israel.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus tells the woman to take comfort, that her faith has made her whole, and bids her go in peace.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus cries out against a faithless and perverse generation, asking how long he will bear with them, and bids the father bring his son.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus asks whether, when the Son of Man comes, he will find faith on earth, and blesses those who have not seen and yet believed.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus declares that the work of God is to believe in the one whom he has sent.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus tells the crowd that they have seen him and yet do not believe.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus seeks out the man cast out by the Pharisees and asks whether he believes in the Son of God.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus tells the Jews that they do not believe because they are not of his sheep.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus tells the disciples plainly that Lazarus is dead, and is glad for their sakes that they may believe, then bids them go to him.

subcat: The Nature and Power of Faith
text: Jesus declares that whoever believes in him will do the works he does, and greater works, because he goes to the Father.
Jesus calls out to the disciples on the storm-tossed sea, telling them to take heart, that it is he, and not to be afraid.
Jesus rebukes the disciples as of little faith for worrying they have no bread, asking whether they remember the loaves of the five thousand and the four thousand and the baskets they took up.
Jesus cries out against a faithless and perverse generation, asking how long he will bear with them, and bids the boy be brought to him.
Jesus tells the disciples, let us cross over to the other side of the sea.
Jesus asks his disciples why they are so fearful and have no faith, calls Peter of little faith asking why he doubted, and tells the synagogue ruler not to be afraid but only believe.
Jesus calls out as he walks on the sea, telling the disciples to take heart, it is he, do not be afraid.
Jesus tells his disciples, fear not, little flock — it is the Father's good pleasure to give them the kingdom, and charges Thomas to believe.
Jesus says to the nobleman that unless they see signs and wonders, they will not believe.
Jesus calls out to the terrified disciples on the sea, telling them it is he and not to be afraid.

Jesus charges his hearers to take no thought for life, food, drink, or clothing, declaring that life is more than food and the body more than clothing, and that the heavenly Father knows they need all these things.

Jesus bids his hearers consider the birds the Father feeds though they neither sow nor reap, and the lilies arrayed beyond Solomon. If God so clothes the grass, he asks, will he not much more clothe you of little faith.

Jesus charges his hearers to seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to them, taking no thought for tomorrow, for sufficient to the day is its own trouble.

Jesus tells his disciples that when they are handed over they should take no thought how or what to speak, for it will be given them in that hour, since it is not they who speak but the Spirit of their Father.

Jesus tells his disciples not to let their hearts be troubled, leaves his peace not as the world gives, and declares that in the world they will have tribulation but take heart, for he has overcome the world.

Jesus declares he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfill them. Not one jot or tittle will pass till all is fulfilled, and whoever breaks the least commandment will be called least in the kingdom of heaven.
Jesus answers the lawyer's question with a question, asking what is written in the law and how he reads it.
Jesus declares that the law and the prophets were until John, and that since then the kingdom of God is preached and every man presses into it.
Jesus declares that it is easier for heaven and earth to pass than for one tittle of the law to fail.

subcat: Moses and the Scriptures Pointing to Jesus
text: Jesus says that if his hearers had believed Moses they would have believed him, for Moses wrote of him, and asks how they will believe his words if they do not believe his writings.

subcat: Moses and the Scriptures Pointing to Jesus
text: Jesus declares that their father Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and that he saw it and was glad.

At the Last Supper Jesus gives the disciples bread and the cup as his body and his blood of the new covenant poured out for many for the remission of sins, charging them to do this in remembrance of him.
Jesus declares that the cup is his blood of the new covenant, poured out for many for the remission of sins.
Jesus pledges he will not drink of the fruit of the vine again until the day he drinks it new with his disciples in his Father's kingdom.

subcat: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
text: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman that if she knew the gift of God and who was speaking, she would have asked him for living water.

subcat: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
text: Jesus says whoever drinks of this well water will thirst again.

subcat: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
text: Jesus corrects the crowd that not Moses but his Father gives the true bread from heaven, which comes down and gives life to the world.

subcat: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
text: Jesus declares he is the bread of life — the living bread from heaven whose flesh he will give for the life of the world.

subcat: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
text: Jesus says their fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died, but the bread that comes down from heaven lets one eat and not die.

subcat: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
text: Jesus declares that unless they eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, they have no life in them.

subcat: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
text: Jesus says whoever eats his flesh and drinks his blood has eternal life and will be raised up at the last day, for his flesh is true food and his blood true drink; such a one abides in him and he in them.

subcat: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
text: Jesus promises that whoever feeds on him will live by him forever, unlike the fathers who ate manna and died.

subcat: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching
text: Jesus clarifies that the Spirit gives life and the flesh profits nothing — the words he speaks are spirit and life.

subcat: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer
text: Jesus teaches his disciples to pray this way, addressing God as their Father in heaven and hallowing his name.

subcat: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer
text: Jesus prays for the Father's kingdom to come and his will to be done on earth as it is in heaven.

subcat: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer
text: Jesus asks the Father to give us this day our daily bread.

subcat: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer
text: Jesus prays that the Father would forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors.

subcat: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer
text: Jesus prays that the Father would lead us not into temptation but deliver us from evil, for his is the kingdom, power, and glory forever.
Jesus charges his disciples not to pray like hypocrites in public, but to enter their room and pray to the Father in secret.
Jesus warns against vain repetitions, for the Father knows what his children need before they ask him.
Jesus tells his disciples that when they stand praying they must forgive any grievance, that the Father in heaven may forgive their trespasses.

Jesus charges his hearers to ask and it will be given, seek and they will find, knock and it will be opened, for everyone who asks receives, and asks what father would give his son a stone for bread or a serpent for a fish.
Jesus tells his disciples that this kind can come forth by nothing but by prayer and fasting.
Jesus promises that whatever his disciples ask in his name he will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
Jesus tells his disciples he chose them to bear lasting fruit, that whatever they ask the Father in his name he may give them.
Jesus tells his disciples a time comes when he will speak plainly of the Father, and in that day they will ask in his name.
